title: SPARK CSEC Mathematics - Paper 02 Practice Paper B
instructions: This paper consists of THREE sections: I, II and III.
Section I has THREE questions; Section II has THREE questions and Section III has THREE questions.
Numerical answers that are non-exact should be given correct to 3 significant figures or 1 decimal place for angles in degrees, unless a different level of accuracy is specified in the question.
All working MUST be clearly shown.
A table of formulae is provided.
Diagrams are NOT drawn to scale, unless otherwise stated.

questions.topic: Computation in standard form, currency exchange and consumer arithmetic

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Determine the value of the following, giving your answer in standard form.

(0.36 x 0.055)/sqrt(0.09 x 25)

criteria.description: the value of the expression
the value written in standard form

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows the rates of exchange at a commercial bank in Kingston.

US$1.00 = JA$156.00
CAN$1.00 = JA$120.00

Using the table, calculate the CAN equivalent of US$1.00.

criteria.description: finding the CAN equivalent of JA$1.00
multiplying the CAN equivalent of JA$1.00 by 156.00

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Mr Palmer's daughter, who is a student in Canada, sent him CAN$871.00, which he exchanged for US dollars. Calculate the amount received in US dollars.

criteria.description: dividing by the CAN equivalent of US$1.00

parts.label: (c) (i)
parts.prompt:
Mr Palmer is paid a basic wage of $18.50 per hour for a 40-hour week. Overtime is paid at time-and-a-half. In one week he worked 47 hours.

Calculate his TOTAL wage for that week.
parts.solution: His basic wage is 40 x $18.50 = $740.00. Overtime is paid at 1.5 x $18.50 = $27.75 per hour, and he worked 47 - 40 = 7 hours of overtime, earning 7 x $27.75 = $194.25. His total wage is $740.00 + $194.25 = $934.25.

criteria.description: finding the overtime pay for 7 hours at $27.75 per hour
the total wage

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: In the following week Mr Palmer's total wage was $1 017.50. Determine the TOTAL number of hours that he worked in that week.
parts.solution: His overtime pay was $1 017.50 - $740.00 = $277.50, so the number of hours of overtime is 277.50/27.75 = 10. He therefore worked 40 + 10 = 50 hours in that week.

criteria.description: subtracting the basic wage and dividing by the overtime rate
the total number of hours

questions.stem: Kemar uses matchsticks of length 1 cm to make a row of squares. Figure 1 is a single square, Figure 2 is a row of 2 squares sharing a side, Figure 3 is a row of 3 squares, and the pattern continues.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows the number of matchsticks used and the perimeter of each figure. Some rows have not been included.

Study the pattern of numbers in each row of the table. Complete the table by filling in the missing information.
parts.solution: The first square uses 4 matchsticks and each further square adds 3, so Figure n uses 3n + 1. Figure 4 uses 3(4) + 1 = 13 and Figure 7 uses 3(7) + 1 = 22. The figure is a 1 cm by n cm rectangle, so its perimeter is 2(n + 1) = 2n + 2: Figure 4 gives 10 cm and Figure 7 gives 16 cm.

mn.description: matchsticks in Figure n, in terms of n

pn.description: perimeter of Figure n, in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt: Kemar has 100 matchsticks. Determine the greatest number of squares that can be made in a single row.
parts.solution: 3n + 1 <= 100 gives 3n <= 99, so n <= 33. The greatest whole number of squares is 33, which uses 3(33) + 1 = 100 matchsticks.

criteria.description: forms 3n + 1 <= 100
the greatest number of squares

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Write a formula in terms of n for the AREA, in square centimetres, enclosed by Figure n.
parts.solution: Each square encloses 1 cm^2 and Figure n is a row of n squares, so the area enclosed is n cm^2.

criteria.description: the area in terms of n

questions.topic: Factorisation, binary operations, sets and scale drawing

parts.label: (a) (i)
parts.prompt:
Factorize completely

4x^2y + 10xy^3.
parts.solution: Both terms have a factor of 2, a factor of x and a factor of y, so the common factor is 2xy. 4x^2y + 10xy^3 = 2xy(2x + 5y^2).

criteria.description: the complete factorisation

parts.label: (a) (ii) a)
parts.prompt:
If a * b = 2a + 3b, calculate the value of

4 * 3.

criteria.description: the value of 4 * 3

parts.label: (a) (ii) b)
parts.prompt:
Hence, calculate the value of

(4 * 3) * 2.

criteria.description: substituting the value of 4 * 3 back into the operation

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of x.
parts.solution: The four regions account for every one of the 40 members, so (24 - x) + x + (22 - x) + 3 = 40. That is 49 - x = 40, so x = 49 - 40 = 9.

parts.label: (c) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the ACTUAL area, in km^2, of the forest reserve, given that 1 x 10^10 cm^2 = 1 km^2.
parts.solution: The forest reserve covers 15 of the small squares, so its area on the map is 15 cm^2. parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: Determine the median number of tickets sold over the six days.
parts.solution: Arranged in order, the six values are 20, 30, 40, 50, 70, 90. The median is the mean of the third and fourth of these, that is (40 + 50) divided by 2, which is 45.

criteria.description: the median of the six values

parts.label: (a) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean number of tickets sold over the six days.
parts.solution: The six values total 30 + 70 + 20 + 90 + 50 + 40 = 300. The mean is therefore 300 divided by 6, which is 50.

criteria.description: the total of the six values, 300
the mean

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
A sports store sells cricket bats and cricket balls. In June it sold 30 bats and 45 balls, and in July it sold 26 bats and 52 balls.

Write a 2 x 2 matrix, N, to represent this information, using the rows for June and July and the columns for bats and balls.
parts.solution: The two rows are June and July and the two columns are bats and balls, so N = [[30, 45], [26, 52]].

criteria.description: the matrix N

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt:
A cricket bat costs $250.00 and a cricket ball costs $80.00.

Write a 2 x 1 matrix, C, to represent the cost, in dollars, of one bat and of one ball.
parts.solution: C is a column matrix with one entry for each of the two items, in the same order as the columns of N, so C = [[250], [80]].

criteria.description: the matrix C, with the correct rows and columns

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the matrix product NC.

criteria.description: multiplying each row of N by the column C
the matrix product NC

parts.label: (b) (iv)
parts.prompt: State, giving a reason for your answer, whether the matrix product CN can be found.
parts.answer: No. CN cannot be found, because C has 1 column and N has 2 rows, so the two matrices are not conformable in that order
parts.solution: C is a 2 x 1 matrix and N is a 2 x 2 matrix. A product can only be found when the number of columns of the first matrix equals the number of rows of the second. C has 1 column and N has 2 rows, so CN cannot be found. (NC can be found, and is the product calculated in (b) (iii).)

rubric.description: says that CN cannot be found because C has 1 column and N has 2 rows

questions.topic: Geometric construction and trigonometry in right-angled triangles

parts.label: (a) (i)
parts.prompt:
The line AB, 10 cm long, is drawn on the construction pad.

Using only a ruler and a pair of compasses, construct the perpendicular bisector of AB. Your construction arcs must be clearly shown.
parts.answer: the perpendicular bisector of AB, with the four construction arcs left on the page
parts.solution: Open the compasses to more than half of AB, that is to more than 5 cm. With centre A, draw arcs above and below AB. With the SAME radius and centre B, draw two more arcs to cut them. Rule the straight line through the two points where the arcs cross: that line is the perpendicular bisector of AB. The arcs must be left on the page.

parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: Your bisector cuts AB at the point M. State, giving a reason for your answer, the length of AM.
parts.answer: AM = 5 cm, because the perpendicular bisector of AB cuts AB at its midpoint, so AM is half of AB
parts.solution: The perpendicular bisector of a line segment passes through the midpoint of that segment, so M is the midpoint of AB and AM = MB. AB = 10 cm, so AM is half of 10 cm, that is 5 cm.

rubric.description: states 5 cm and says that the bisector cuts AB at its midpoint

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The diagram below shows a right-angled triangle KLM with sides p units, q units and r units, and angle KLM = 90°.

Using the diagram, write, in terms of q and r, an expression for sin θ.
parts.solution: θ is the angle at M. The side opposite θ is KL, of length q, and the hypotenuse is MK, of length r. So sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = q/r.

The angle at L, between KL and LM, is marked as a right angle. The hypotenuse MK runs from M up to K and is marked r units. The angle at M, between LM and MK, is marked with an arc and labelled θ.

criteria.description: the ratio sin θ = q/r

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Using the result from (b) (i), show that (sin θ)/(cos θ) = q/p.
parts.solution: sin θ = q/r and cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = p/r. So (sin θ)/(cos θ) = (q/r)/(p/r). The r in the numerator and the r in the denominator cancel, leaving (sin θ)/(cos θ) = q/p.

criteria.description: substituting sin θ = q/r and cos θ = p/r
cancelling r to reach q/p

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Given that q = 7 units and p = 24 units, calculate the size of angle θ, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.solution: From (b) (ii), (sin θ)/(cos θ) = tan θ = q/p = 7/24. So θ = the angle whose tangent is 7/24, which is 16.3°.

criteria.description: using tan θ = q/p = 7/24
the size of angle θ

questions.topic: Coordinate geometry, functions and the graph of a quadratic

parts.label: (a) (i)
parts.prompt:
The line RS passes through the points R(-2, -1) and S(2, 7).

Determine the equation of the line RS.
parts.solution: The gradient of RS is m = (7 - (-1))/(2 - (-2)), that is 8/4 = 2. Using y = mx + c with S(2, 7): 7 = 2(2) + c, so c = 3. The equation of RS is y = 2x + 3.

criteria.description: the gradient of RS
the equation of the line RS

parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: Determine the equation of the line which passes through S and which is perpendicular to the line RS.
parts.solution: The gradient of RS is 2, so the gradient of a line perpendicular to RS is -1/2 = -1/2. Using y = mx + c with S(2, 7): 7 = (-1/2)(2) + c, so c = 8. The equation of the line is y = -(1/2)x + 8.

criteria.description: the gradient of the perpendicular line
the equation of the perpendicular line

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The functions f and g are defined as

f(x) = 3x - 4   and   g(x) = (3x - 1)/(x + 2), x != -2.

Determine the value of gf(3).

criteria.description: evaluating f(3) and substituting it into g
the value of gf(3)

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Derive a simplified expression for g^(-1)(x).
parts.solution: Let y = g(x), so y = (3x - 1)/(x + 2). Interchanging x and y gives x = (3y - 1)/(y + 2), so x(y + 2) = 3y - 1. Expanding the left-hand side, xy + 2x = 3y - 1. Collecting the terms in y on one side gives xy - 3y = -2x - 1, that is y(x - 3) = -2x - 1. Dividing by x - 3 gives g^(-1)(x) = (2x + 1)/(3 - x).

criteria.description: interchanging x and y and clearing the fraction
the correct inverse

parts.label: (c) (i)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows values of y = x^2 - 4x + 3 for -1 <= x <= 5.

x     -1    0    1    2    3    4    5
y      8    3    0   -1    0    3    8

Using a scale of 2 cm to represent 1 unit on the x-axis and 1 cm to represent 1 unit on the y-axis, plot the points in the table and draw the graph of y = x^2 - 4x + 3 for -1 <= x <= 5.
parts.answer: the points (-1, 8), (0, 3), (1, 0), (2, -1), (3, 0), (4, 3), (5, 8) joined by a smooth curve
parts.solution: Plot the seven points from the table: (-1, 8), (0, 3), (1, 0), (2, -1), (3, 0), (4, 3), (5, 8). Join them with a single smooth curve - a parabola with its lowest point at (2, -1) - and do not join them with straight line segments.

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: Using your graph, state the coordinates of the minimum point of the function
parts.solution: The lowest point of the curve drawn is at (2, -1), so the minimum point is (2, -1).

criteria.description: the coordinates of the minimum point

parts.label: (c) (iii)
parts.prompt: Using your graph, state the solutions of the equation x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0.

parts.label: (a) (iii)
parts.prompt: Using a vector method, show that AB is parallel to CD.
parts.answer: AB = [[6], [8]] and CD = [[3], [4]], so CD = 1/2 AB. CD is a scalar multiple of AB, so AB is parallel to CD
parts.solution: AB = OB - OA = [[2], [7]] - [[-4], [-1]] = [[6], [8]], and CD = OD - OC = [[7], [2]] - [[4], [-2]] = [[3], [4]]. Then CD = 1/2 AB, so CD is a scalar multiple of AB. Two vectors that are scalar multiples of each other have the same direction, so AB is parallel to CD.

rubric.description: shows that CD = 1/2 AB, that is, that one vector is a scalar multiple of the other
concludes that AB is parallel to CD

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The matrix M = [[2, 5], [1, 3]].

Evaluate the determinant of M.

criteria.description: the determinant of M

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt:
The simultaneous equations

2x + 5y = 4
1x + 3y = 3

may be written as a matrix equation. Write this matrix equation.
parts.solution: The coefficients form M, the unknowns form the column [[x], [y]] and the constants form the column [[4], [3]], so the matrix equation is [[2, 5], [1, 3]][[x], [y]] = [[4], [3]].

rubric.description: writes M multiplied by the column of unknowns equal to the column of constants

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Using a matrix method, solve for x and y.
parts.solution: The determinant of M is 1, so M is non-singular and M^-1 = [[3, -5], [-1, 2]]. Multiplying both sides of the matrix equation on the left by M^-1 gives [[x], [y]] = [[3, -5], [-1, 2]][[4], [3]] = [[-3], [2]]. So x = -3 and y = 2.

criteria.description: finds M^-1 and multiplies the column of constants by it
the values of x and y

parts.prompt:
In the diagram below, A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. The line TA is a tangent to the circle at A, and angle TAB = 64°.

Calculate, giving a reason for your answer, the measure of angle ACB.
parts.solution: The angle between the tangent TA and the chord AB is equal to the angle in the alternate segment, which is the angle ACB subtended by AB at the circumference on the other side of the chord. So angle ACB = angle TAB = 64°.

parts.solution: Angle AOB is the angle at the centre subtended by the arc AB, and angle ACB is the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc. The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so angle AOB = 2 x 64 = 128°.

parts.prompt: Determine the measure of angle OAB.
parts.solution: OA and OB are radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles and angle OAB = angle OBA. The angles of the triangle add to 180°, so angle OAB = (180 - 128) / 2 = 26°.

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt:
R is 50 km from Q, on a bearing of 250°.

parts.solution: The bearing of P from Q is 325° and the bearing of R from Q is 250°, so angle PQR = 325° - 250° = 75°. By the cosine rule, PR^2 = 80^2 + 50^2 - 2(80)(50) cos 75 = 6400 + 2500 - 8000 cos 75 = 6829.45. So PR = sqrt(6829.45) = 82.6405 = 82.6 km, correct to 3 significant figures.

substitutes into the cosine rule
the distance PR

The masses of 50 parcels handled at a courier depot in one morning were recorded.

The table below shows the masses, in kilograms, and the cumulative frequencies. Complete the table by inserting the TWO missing values in the cumulative frequency column.
parts.solution: Each cumulative frequency is the running total of the frequencies up to and including that class: 6, 20, 38, 46, 50. So the two missing values are 38 and 46.

table.caption: Masses of 50 parcels handled at a depot.

c2.description: the cumulative frequency up to 15 kg

c3.description: the cumulative frequency up to 20 kg

parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: Using a scale of 2 cm to represent 5 kg on the horizontal axis and 2 cm to represent 10 parcels on the vertical axis, draw the cumulative frequency curve for the data. Start your curve at (0, 0).
parts.answer: the points (0, 0), (5, 6), (10, 20), (15, 38), (20, 46), (25, 50) joined by a smooth curve
parts.solution: The cumulative frequency is plotted against the UPPER CLASS BOUNDARY of each class, not the midpoint, and the curve starts at (0, 0) because no member of the sample falls below the first boundary. Plot (0, 0), (5, 6), (10, 20), (15, 38), (20, 46), (25, 50) and join them with a single smooth curve that never falls.

parts.label: (a) (iii)
parts.prompt: Using your graph, estimate the probability that a parcel chosen at random has a mass of MORE than 15 kg.
parts.solution: From the curve, 38 of the 50 parcels have a mass of 15 kg or less, so 50 - 38 = 12 of them have a mass of more than 15 kg. The probability is therefore 12/50 = 6/25.

criteria.description: the probability, read from the candidate's own curve

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration of the cyclist during the first 8 seconds.
parts.solution: During the first 8 seconds the speed changes from 4 m/s to 24 m/s, a change of 20 m/s, and it takes 8 seconds. The acceleration is the gradient of that stage of the graph: the change in speed divided by the time taken, which is 2.5 m/s^2.

criteria.description: uses the gradient of that stage of the graph
the acceleration

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the TOTAL distance travelled by the cyclist during the 20 seconds.
parts.solution: The distance travelled is the area under the speed-time graph. The graph is never at rest while the speed is changing, so that stage is a TRAPEZIUM and not a triangle: the trapezium from 0 s to 8 s has area 1/2(4 + 24)(8) = 112; the trapezium from 8 s to 20 s has area 1/2(24 + 0)(12) = 144. The total distance is therefore 256 m.

criteria.description: treats the distance as the area under the graph, taking the sloping stage as a trapezium and not as the triangle underneath it
the total distance

parts.label: (b) (iv)
parts.prompt: Describe the motion of the cyclist during the last 12 seconds.
parts.answer: The cyclist decelerates uniformly from 24 m/s and comes to rest at the end of the 20 seconds
parts.solution: The cyclist decelerates uniformly from 24 m/s and comes to rest at the end of the 20 seconds.
